# Codexa Scanner — Product & Engineering Todo

Last reviewed: 2026-11-17  
Repository: `hidecard/codexa-scanner`  
Current baseline: commit `75ef9cf` — responsive UI/scrollbar improvements.  
Status rule: `[x]` verified complete; `[ ]` not complete; `[~]` partial/in progress; `[=]` already exists and should not be reimplemented; `[-]` intentionally deferred/not required for the current release scope.

## Review policy

For each item, first check the current code and tests, decide whether the work is needed, implement only the smallest justified change, run the closest tests, then update this file with the result. Existing features are not counted as new work. Security behavior must preserve authorized use of private/lab networks while making scope explicit; do not silently disable legitimate assessment workflows.

## Phase 1 — Backend stability & target safety (Critical)

**Review:** Required before calling the app production-ready. P1.1 bounds port-scan resources and protects lifecycle state; P1.2 pins a stable resolved address; P1.3 validates bare IP/hostname targets and requires authorization confirmation for a single target plus selected port range; P1.4 constrains HTTP redirect/DNS scope; P1.5 distinguishes legacy TLS support from inconclusive probe failures. Remaining in this phase: consistent frontend error states. Preserve scanning of authorized private/lab hosts; do not add a blanket private-IP deny rule.

- [x] **P1.1 Bound scan inputs and make scan lifecycle concurrency-safe.** Capped workers at 512 and dial timeout at 30 seconds; each scan now has its own context; active-scan state is mutex-protected; overlapping starts are rejected; cancellation closes active banner connections; completed/cancelled/failed terminal states are reflected in the UI. Tests cover limits, active-start rejection, cancellation, and completed/cancelled status.
- [x] **P1.2 Use stable target resolution.** Context-aware, five-second-bounded lookup resolves once per scan; IPv4 and IPv6 literals skip DNS. Hostname answers are deterministically ordered (IPv4 first, then numeric address order), one address is pinned for every port, and the UI shows it. Multiple DNS answers are not all scanned in this iteration because that would require per-address findings/history changes. Tests cover multiple answers, literal IPv4/IPv6, lookup errors, and cancellation during lookup.
- [x] **P1.3 Validate port-scan targets and introduce explicit scope controls.** A scan's scope is the single validated target plus selected port range. The one-shot UI confirmation resets when the target/range changes and is enforced by the Go API. Bare IPv4/IPv6 (including scoped IPv6) and ASCII DNS hostnames are accepted; URL syntax, embedded ports, malformed labels, ambiguous numeric-only hosts, non-ASCII hostnames, and control characters are rejected. Authorized private/lab targets remain allowed. Tests cover accepted/rejected targets and missing scope confirmation.
- [x] **P1.4 Validate HTTP redirect destinations and DNS resolution.** Each submitted URL defines its own hostname/port scope; same-host redirects and standard HTTPâ†’HTTPS 80â†’443 upgrades are allowed, while cross-host redirects, HTTPS downgrades, and out-of-scope ports are blocked. Private/LAN/loopback targets require a default-off one-shot opt-in for authorized labs. The complete DNS answer set is validated, one deterministic address is pinned through the redirect chain, and ambient proxies are bypassed. Link-local, unspecified, multicast, and special-use/reserved addresses remain blocked. Added address-policy, mixed-answer, private opt-in, cross-host redirect, DNS pinning, and hop-limit regression tests.
- [x] **P1.5 Report TLS 1.0/1.1 probes as Supported / Not supported / Inconclusive.** A version-specific handshake means Supported; only an explicit peer `protocol_version` alert means Not supported. Timeouts, network failures, other TLS alerts, or unexpected negotiation are Inconclusive and retain their diagnostic. The TLS UI shows each status and its error; tests cover supported, explicit rejection, handshake failure, timeout, and unexpected-version outcomes.
- [x] **P1.6 Make frontend loading/error handling consistent.** Added `try/catch/finally` around asynchronous scan, analyzer, recon, and history calls; loading flags now reset on failures and actionable errors reach the UI. Added retry-friendly error banners and history loading state.

**Not required in this phase:** Replacing Go/Wails/React/SQLite, a blanket ban on private targets, a proxy/VPN feature, or a large backend directory move. Those add scope without resolving the concrete stability/security defects above.

Avoid duplicate implementations. New visualizations and historical DNS/certificate comparisons are useful follow-ups but not prerequisites for safe scanning.

- [-] Network topology graph — defer until the scanner collects trustworthy host-to-host relationship data; current scan results do not justify a topology map.

## Phase 9 — Modern Stack & Client-Side Exposure Audit (High)

**Review:** Modern and AI-generated ("vibe-coded") web applications frequently expose client-side secrets, source maps, internal API routes, unsafe DOM sinks, or permissive BaaS/CORS configurations. Keep all checks passive or strictly bounded (`HEAD`/capped `GET`), avoid active exploit payloads, redact matched secret values before display or persistence, and report clues rather than attempting exploitation.

- [x] **P9.1 Client-side JS bundle and secret pattern scanner (passive).** Extracts first-party `<script src="...">` URLs from bounded HTML responses and fetches up to 5 scripts (512 KiB each) through the existing scoped HTTP client. Matches common credential/token patterns (e.g. `sk-proj`/OpenAI-like, `sk_live_`, `AIza`, AWS Access Key IDs, GitHub tokens, Supabase `service_role` JWT clues) with regex heuristics; displays/stores only redacted previews with script URL context and adds high-severity passive clue findings.
- [x] **P9.2 Source map and debug artifact detection.** Inspects fetched JS bundles for trailing `//# sourceMappingURL=...` directives and issues a single bounded same-origin `HEAD` check on the resolved map URL to report whether production source maps are publicly reachable (medium-severity clue when reachable).
- [x] **P9.3 Frontend API route and BaaS endpoint extractor.** Parses bounded JS bundles for internal API paths (`/api/...`, `/v1/...`, `/trpc/...`, `/graphql`, etc.) and cloud/BaaS host references (`*.supabase.co`, `*.firebaseio.com`, S3 bucket URLs), surfacing same-origin paths as discovery clues/candidates for authorized Web Audit or Path Discovery.
- [x] **P9.4 CORS and JWT configuration posture audit.** Passive CORS checks include `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` (info), wildcard + credentials misconfiguration (high), and unsafe origin reflection clue when request `Origin` is echoed in `ACAO` without `Vary: Origin` (medium/high if credentials enabled). Passive JWT header/payload metadata decoding from observed response headers/cookies flags `alg:none` or missing `exp`/`nbf` claims without signature verification/brute-forcing; token values are redacted from evidence.
- [x] **P9.5 Framework-specific path discovery presets.** Curated `HEAD`-only path preset sets in Path Fuzzer UI (Next.js, Vite/SPA, Laravel, Django, Spring, plus general env/VCS/API/debug paths) help discover common exposure routes within authorized scope.
- [x] **P9.6 Passive DOM XSS sink and database error disclosure checks.** Passive sampled database error signature detection in HTTP responses (`SQL syntax`, `mysql_fetch`, `PG::SyntaxError`, `ORA-`, `SQLite3::SQLException`, SQLSTATE/PDO/MongoDB clues) as disclosure findings, and bounded JS bundle DOM sink scanning (`dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, `document.write`, `eval`) with script URL/line context (clues only, no data-flow analysis).
- [x] **P9.7 Harmless reflected parameter indicator (passive/non-exploitative).** When an audited URL contains existing query parameters, performs a bounded probe appending a benign alphanumeric marker and reports whether it is echoed unencoded in the sampled HTML body as a passive reflection clue (paired with observed CSP/cookie posture context in results; not proof of exploitability).

All existing target validation, private-network checks, and concurrency limits apply.
- [x] **P10.4 Passive version-to-CVE advisory matcher.** Match observed service banners, `Server`/`X-Powered-By` headers, and generator metadata against a bundled offline advisory dataset to highlight outdated versions with upgrade guidance. Implemented with bundled advisory.json dataset (20+ products, 30+ CVEs), version extraction from SSH/HTTP/FTP/SMTP/MySQL/PostgreSQL/Redis/MongoDB banners, Server header parsing, X-Powered-By parsing, technology fingerprint matching, TLS version checks; version comparison logic for semantic versions; advisory matches added to CIDRHostResult and BulkHeaderResult with source attribution; Wails bindings regenerated; all tests pass.

Added `TakeoverClue` struct and `TakeoverClues` field to `SubdomainResult`. Wails bindings regenerated; all tests pass.
- [x] **P11.3 HTTP protocol and TLS 1.2 weak cipher checks.** Report HTTP/2 from negotiated ALPN, HTTP/3 as an `Alt-Svc` h3 advertisement (without claiming a QUIC handshake), and flag negotiated or accepted legacy TLS 1.2 weak ciphers (CBC, 3DES, RC4, NULL) in TLS Inspector.
